claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure with approximately 2 μm interlamellar spacing.
The as-cast alloy has low room-temperature tensile ductility and suffers catastrophic interfacial cracking.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation will introduce a high dislocation density and break the continuity of the B2 lamellae.
SPD followed by a controlled low-temperature anneal will transform the continuous lamellar B2 phase into a patterned, discontinuous B2 network in an FCC matrix.
A 600–800 °C anneal for 1–4 hours will stabilize fragmented B2 without causing significant coarsening.
A true deformation strain greater than 4 is sufficient to fully fragment the lamellae.
Vacuum or inert-gas annealing will prevent oxidation during the proposed treatment.
A continuous ordered B2 phase can cause poor room-temperature ductility by serving as a mechanically unfavorable continuous phase.
Continuous B2 lamellae in this alloy act as crack-propagation paths and stress concentrators.
Coherent precipitate interfaces can facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that cause premature crack initiation.
The B2 interfaces produced by the proposed treatment will be coherent or semi-coherent.
Dispersing discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous ductile matrix can improve room-temperature ductility while maintaining high strength.
Fragmenting the B2 phase will arrest interfacial cracking and promote uniform plasticity in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile ductility by 30–50%.
The treated alloy will have a room-temperature tensile fracture strain greater than 15%.
The treated alloy will maintain or slightly increase its yield strength to above 800 MPa.
The treatment will eliminate catastrophic interfacial cracking under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Successful annealing requires a temperature below the B2 solvus to avoid dissolution of B2.
Successful deformation requires enough strain to fragment the lamellae without causing amorphization, void formation, or excessive grain growth.
Comparing as-cast, conventional-HIP, and HITM samples can isolate whether the proposed microstructural and tensile changes require the HITM route rather than conventional HIP.
